title: Job's Life Goes From GOATED to Gutted... But He Keeps the Faith
paragraphs: So, there was this guy named Job who lived in a place called Uz. He was, like, a genuinely good dude—super honest, always kept his word, was all-in for God, and absolutely hated seeing bad stuff happen. He had a big family: seven sons and three daughters. And get this—he was loaded. We're talking 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 teams of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a ton of servants. Basically, he was the biggest deal in the entire East.

His sons were all about that party life. They'd take turns throwing these huge feasts at their houses and would always make sure their three sisters were there to hang out. After each round of parties, their dad, Job, would get up super early and offer a sacrifice for each of his kids. He was always thinking, "What if one of my kids messed up and secretly dissed God in their heart?" So, he made this a regular thing, just in case they'd sinned.
Then one day, all the angels went to check in with God, and Satan, who's basically the head accuser, tagged along. God called out Satan specifically, like, "So, what've you been up to?"
Satan shot back, "Just cruising around, you know, checking out what's happening on Earth."
God said to Satan, "Oh yeah? Did you happen to see my boy Job? There's literally no one like him. He's the real deal—honest, a man of his word, totally devoted to me, and hates evil."

Satan just scoffed. "You really think he's that good for nothing? C'mon. The guy has it made! You treat him like a spoiled pet, making sure nothing ever goes wrong for him, his family, or any of his stuff. You bless everything he touches—he literally can't fail.
"But I bet if you actually took away all his stuff, he'd curse you straight to your face. Just watch."
God was like, "Alright, bet. You can do whatever you want with his things. Just don't lay a hand on him." And with that, Satan bounced from God's presence.

Not long after, while Job's kids were partying it up at the oldest brother's house, a messenger sprinted up to Job and said, "We were out in the field, the oxen were plowing and the donkeys were just chilling, when these Sabean raiders attacked! They jacked all the animals and killed all the workers. I'm the only one who made it out to tell you."

Before he could even finish, another messenger ran up, totally out of breath, and said, "Lightning just came out of nowhere and completely fried the sheep and the shepherds. They're all toast. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."

And while HE was still talking, a third guy showed up and said, "A bunch of Chaldean raiders came at us from three different directions, stole all the camels, and killed all the drivers. I'm the only one who got away to tell you."

And if that wasn't enough, while that guy was still talking, a fourth messenger arrived, saying, "Your kids were all hanging out at your oldest son's place when a massive tornado just ripped in from the desert and wrecked the house. It collapsed right on top of them, and they're all… gone. I'm the only one who survived to tell you what happened."
Job just stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground and just started worshiping, saying:
"I came into this world with nothing, and I'll leave with nothing. God gives, and God takes away. But blessed be God's name."
Through all of this absolute chaos, Job didn't sin. Not once did he point a finger and blame God.

title: Job's Ultimate Test: Round 2
paragraphs: So, one day, all the angels were reporting back to God, and guess who decided to show up again? Satan.
God immediately called him out, like, "And what have you been up to?"
Satan shot back, "Oh, you know, just cruising around, checking things out on earth."

Then God was like, "So, have you seen my boy Job? There's literally no one like him. He's honest, keeps his word, is totally devoted to me, and hates doing wrong. He's still holding on strong, even after you tried to get me to ruin him for no reason. Nice try, though."
Satan replied, "Yeah, but a person will give up anything just to save their own skin. What if you actually hurt him? Like, messed with his health? I bet he'd curse you to your face, for real."
God said, "Fine. Do whatever you want to him. Just don't kill him."

So Satan left God's presence and hit Job with some gnarly sores. Job was covered in painful ulcers and scabs from head to toe. They were so itchy and gross that he grabbed a piece of a broken pot to scrape himself and went to go sit in a pile of ashes on the trash heap.
His wife came to him and said, "Are you seriously still trying to be Mr. Perfect? Just curse God and let's be done with this!"
He told her, "You're talking like a fool. We take all the good stuff from God, why shouldn't we take the bad stuff too?"
And through all of this, Job didn't sin. He didn't say a single bad thing about God.

When Job's three best friends heard about all the terrible things that had happened to him, they decided to come and support him. Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuhah, and Zophar from Naamath all traveled to comfort him. But when they first saw him, they couldn't even recognize him. It was wild. They started wailing, tore their clothes, and threw dirt on their heads to show how sad they were. Then they just sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights without saying a word. They could see how completely wrecked he was and how much pain he was in.
changes: Ch2: MSG 1-3 split into 4 EN paras; MSG 10 split into 2 EN paras; splits declared

title: Job's Epic Rant About His Life
paragraphs: Then Job finally broke the silence and started cursing the day he was born.

“Just erase the day I was born. Erase the night I was conceived! Let it be a total black hole. May God just forget it ever happened. Wipe it from the history books! May my birthday be buried in deep darkness, covered by fog, and swallowed by the night. And the night I was conceived—let it disappear too! Rip that date off the calendar, wipe it from every record. Oh, turn that night into pure nothingness—no happy sounds from that night, ever! Let the professional cursers curse that day. Unleash the sea monster, Leviathan, on it. May its morning stars turn black, waiting for a daylight that never shows up, never even seeing the first light of dawn. And why? Because it let me be born from my mother’s womb into a life with this much trouble.

“Why couldn’t I have just died at birth, my first breath being my last? Why were there arms to rock me and a chest to feed me? I could be chilling in peace right now, asleep forever, feeling no pain. I'd be with kings and politicians in their fancy tombs, or with princes surrounded by their gold and silver. Why wasn't I a stillborn baby, buried with all the others who never saw the light of day? A place where the wicked can't bother anyone and tired people finally get to rest. Prisoners sleep without being disturbed, never having to hear a guard yell again. The small and the great are all the same there, and slaves are finally free from their masters.

“Why does God even bother giving light to miserable people? Why keep bitter people alive? People who desperately want to die but can't, who think death is the best thing they could imagine. They'd consider the day they die and get buried the happiest day of their lives. What's the point of life when it makes no sense, when God has blocked every path to meaning?

“Instead of food, I get groans for dinner, and then I just vomit up my pain. My worst nightmare has literally come true; what I was most afraid of has happened. My peace is gone, my quiet is destroyed. There's no rest for me, ever—it feels like death has taken over my life.”
changes: Ch3: badges fixed 1 -> 1-2, 2-10 -> 3-10 (EN para2 covers MSG 3-10 curse content)

title: Your Friend's Advice is... BRUTAL
paragraphs: Then Eliphaz from Teman spoke up:

“Yo, Job, mind if I say something? It’s kinda hard to stay quiet seeing all this. You’ve been the one dishing out advice, helping people see things clearly, and encouraging everyone who was about to quit. Your words have literally put stumbling people back on their feet and given hope to those about to collapse. But now you’re the one in deep trouble, and you’re totally bugging out. You got hit hard and you're reeling from it. But shouldn’t your faith give you some confidence now? Shouldn’t your good-guy life give you some hope?

“Think about it. Has a truly innocent person ever gotten completely wrecked? Do genuinely good people ever really lose in the end? From what I’ve seen, those who stir up trouble and plant seeds of evil get it all back in the end. One breath from God and they’re gone, one blast of his anger and there’s nothing left. The lion might be the king of the jungle, but if he loses his teeth, he’s useless. No teeth, no food, and his cubs are left to fend for themselves.

“I got this secret message, like a whisper, but I heard it crystal clear. It came in a wild dream one night when I was deep asleep. I was hit with this insane dread and terror. I was literally scared to death, shaking from head to toe. A spirit glided right in front of me—the hair on my head stood straight up. I couldn’t even tell what it was, just a blur… and then I heard this muffled voice:

“‘How can a regular person be more righteous than God? How can a human be purer than their own Creator? Look, God doesn’t even fully trust his own servants or give his angels a free pass. So how much less us, who are just made of dust and as fragile as moths? Our bodies are here today and gone tomorrow, and no one even notices—gone without a trace. When the tent stakes of our life are pulled up, the whole thing collapses—we die without ever getting any wiser.’”
changes: Ch4: split declared for MSG 1-6 (intro + body)

title: Why Bad Things Happen & How to Deal
paragraphs: “Go ahead, Job, call for help if you think anyone’s gonna answer. Which of the holy angels are you gonna hit up? A fool’s hot temper is what gets them in the end, and an idiot’s jealousy is basically a death trap. I’ve seen it myself—I’ve seen fools putting down roots, looking all successful, and then boom, their whole setup is cursed. Their kids are left out in the cold, getting used and abused, with nobody to have their back. Random hungry people just roll up and steal their harvest, taking everything, even the thorny parts. They’re just insatiable for everything they own. Don’t blame fate when things go wrong—trouble doesn’t just appear out of thin air. It’s a human thing. Mortals are born for trouble, as sure as sparks fly up from a fire.

“If I were in your shoes, I’d go straight to God. I’d just throw myself on His mercy. I mean, He’s famous for doing awesome and unexpected stuff; His surprises are endless. For example, He sends rain all over the earth, watering the fields. He lifts up the people who are down and out and gives a solid footing to those who are drowning in sadness. He totally wrecks the plans of sneaky crooks, so none of their plots ever work out. He catches the know-it-alls in their own traps—all their complicated schemes get tossed in the trash. Suddenly they’re all confused, like they’re in total darkness; they can’t even see to walk straight. But God saves the oppressed from all the deadly plots and from the iron fist of the powerful. And that’s why the poor keep on hoping, while injustice gets shut down.

“So, it’s lowkey a blessing when God steps in and corrects you. For real, don’t hate on the discipline of Almighty God! It’s true, He wounds, but He also bandages the wound; the same hand that hurts you is the one that heals you. He’ll rescue you from one disaster after another; no matter what crazy thing happens, the evil can’t even touch you.

“When there’s a famine, He’ll keep you from starving. In a war, He’ll keep you from getting taken out by a sword. You’ll be protected from vicious gossip and you’ll be fearless through any catastrophe. You’ll just shrug off disaster and famine, and walk fearlessly among wild animals. You’ll be on good terms with the rocks and mountains; wild animals will become your friends. You’ll know that your place on earth is safe; you’ll check on all your stuff and find nothing missing. You’ll get to see your children grow up, your family as lovely and graceful as a field of green grass. You’ll live a long, good life and die at a ripe old age, like golden grain ready for harvest.
“Yeah, this is how it is—my word of honor. Take it to heart and you won’t go wrong.”
changes: Ch5: badges fixed 1-8 -> 1-7, 9-16 -> 8-16, 8-27 -> 17-19 (content already matched MSG)

title: Job Claps Back: My Suffering is Heavier Than All The Sand
paragraphs: Job answered:

“If you could actually weigh all my misery, if you could pile up this whole disaster on a scale, it would be heavier than all the sand in the sea! So is it any wonder I’m screaming like a cornered animal? God Almighty’s arrows are stuck in me, they’re poison arrows, and I’m poisoned through and through. God has just dumped his entire wrath on me. Donkeys and cows make noise when they run out of food—so don’t expect me to stay quiet through this. Do you see what God has served me? It’s enough to make anyone’s stomach turn. Everything inside me is repulsed by it—it makes me sick.

“All I want is for one prayer to be answered, a final request: let God just step on me—squash me like a bug, and be done with me for good. At least I’d have the satisfaction of knowing I didn’t blaspheme the Holy God, before being pushed past my breaking point. Where’s the strength to keep my hopes up? What future do I have to keep me going? Do you think I have nerves of steel? Do you think I’m made of iron? Do you think I can just fix this myself? Bro, I don’t even have the tools to start!

“When desperate people give up on God Almighty, their friends, at least, should stick with them. But you guys, my 'brothers,' are as unreliable as a desert stream—one day you’re overflowing with water from melting snow, but by summer you’re completely bone-dry, just a baked gully in the sun. Travelers who see you from a distance and detour for a drink end up in a waterless ditch and die of thirst. Merchant caravans from Tema see you and expect water, tourists from Sheba hope for a cool drink. They show up so confident—but what a letdown! They get there, and their faces just fall. And you, my so-called friends, are just like that—you’re useless! You take one look at a tough situation and you shrink back in fear. It’s not like I asked you for anything—I didn’t ask you for a single coin. Nor did I beg you to risk your necks for me. So why are you being so shady and evasive?

“Just hit me with the truth and I’ll shut up. Show me where I went wrong. Honest words never hurt, but what’s the point of all your preachy nonsense? You act like you're correcting me, but you treat my words of pure agony like they're just hot air. Are people just objects to you? Are friends just another item on your ledger?

“Look me in the eyes! Do you really think I’d lie to your face? Think about it—no more double-talk. Think carefully—my integrity is on the line here! Can you find anything fake in what I’m saying? Don’t you trust me to know the difference between right and wrong?”
changes: Ch6: badge 29-30 -> 28-30 (EN para covers MSG 28-30 fully)

title: God, Just Let Me BREATHE
paragraphs: “Isn’t life just one big struggle? Like, we’re all sentenced to a life of hard work. It’s like being a field hand just waiting for the day to be over, or some worker who’s only got payday to look forward to. That’s my life right now, just pointless months and miserable nights. I go to bed thinking, ‘When is it morning already?’ I just toss and turn all night, and I’m so over it. I’m literally covered in gross stuff, my skin’s all messed up and nasty. My days are flying by faster than someone speed-knitting, and then suddenly the yarn’s gone—my life’s unfinished.

“God, seriously, don’t forget I’m just... temporary. Like a puff of smoke. My eyes have seen the last good thing they’re ever gonna see. And you’ve seen the last of me. Even as you’re looking, I’m fading away. Like a cloud that just disappears, people who die don’t come back. They don’t visit their families, their friends don’t just drop by for a chat anymore.

“So yeah, I’m not holding back. I’m putting it all out there. My complaining is bitter, but it’s real. Are you gonna try and shut me up, like you do with the sea and the storms? If I think, ‘Maybe if I just go to sleep, I’ll feel better,’ you just send me nightmares and freak me out with ghosts. Honestly, I’d rather just suffocate than keep living like this. I hate my life! Who needs this? Just leave me alone! My life is nothing, just smoke.

“Like, what even are humans that you care so much? That you even give us the time of day? You check on us every single morning, like ‘how’s it going down there?’ Just give me a break, will you? Can’t you let me even spit in peace? And even if I did sin, how does that even affect you? You’re in charge of everyone. Don’t you have better things to do than to pick on me? Why are you making such a big deal out of me? Why not just forgive me and let’s start over? At this rate, I’ll be dead soon. You’ll look for me, but I’ll be gone.”

title: God Doesn't Mess Up, Bro
paragraphs: Bildad from Shuhah had to jump in next:

"Bro, how can you keep talking like that? You're just spouting nonsense, and it's loud nonsense too. You think God messes up? That the Almighty ever gets things backward? It's lowkey obvious your kids sinned against him—why else would God have punished them? So here's the move—and don't sleep on it: get on your knees and pray to God Almighty. If you're as innocent and good as you say you are, it's not too late. He'll pull up, make everything right again, and restore your life. Even though you're not doing so hot right now, you'll end up better than ever.

"Go ask your ancestors, for real. Study what they learned from their own ancestors. 'Cause we're new to this, with a lot to learn and not much time to learn it. So why not let the old-timers teach you, tell you what's real, and give you the wisdom they got from experience? Can huge pine trees grow without any dirt? Can you get juicy tomatoes without any water? Flowers look pretty before you pick them, but without soil or water, they die faster than grass. That's exactly what happens to people who forget God—all their dreams just crash and burn. They're basically hanging on by a single thread, trusting a spider web to save them. One little shake and the thread snaps, one poke and the whole web is gone. Or they're like weeds that pop up in the sun, taking over the whole garden, choking out the flowers, and even growing in the rocks. But when the gardener yanks them out, the garden doesn't even notice they're gone. The sooner the godless are out of the picture, the better, so that good things can grow in their place.

"There's no way God would ever ditch a good person, and no way he'd ever help a bad one. God's gonna let you laugh again; you'll be shouting with so much joy, while your enemies are totally owned, their whole world collapsing like a house of cards."

title: God's on a Power Trip & I Can't Even
paragraphs: Job just kept going:

“Seriously, what else is new? I already know all this. The real question is, how can a regular person ever get on the right side of God? If we wanted to take him to court, we wouldn't have a shot—not even one in a thousand. God's wisdom is, like, crazy deep and his power is insane. Who could go up against him and come out okay? He moves mountains before they even know what hit them, just flips them upside down whenever he wants. He shakes the whole planet, rattling it to its core. He can tell the sun not to shine, and it listens. He literally puts the stars on lockdown. He stretched out the heavens all by himself and walks on the ocean waves. He's the one who designed the Big Dipper, Orion, the Pleiades, and all those stars in the southern sky. We can't even begin to get our heads around the awesome things he does; his miracles are just one surprise after another. It's wild because he can move right past me, and I don't even see him. He's working, quiet and steady, and I totally miss it. If he decides to take something from you, who's gonna stop him? Who's gonna be like, ‘Hey, what do you think you're doing?’ God doesn't pull his punches with his anger; even mythical monsters are terrified of him.

“So how could I possibly argue with him? How could I build a case that would actually get through to God? Even if I was completely innocent, I could never prove it. All I can do is beg the Judge for mercy. If I called out to God and he actually answered, that's the only way I'd believe he heard me. But right now, it feels like he's just messing with me, beating me up for no reason at all. He won't even let me catch my breath; it's just one bitter thing after another. If it's a contest of strength, he wins, no question. If it's about justice, who's gonna serve him a subpoena? Even if I'm innocent, anything I say just makes me look guilty. The more I defend myself, the worse I sound, even though I'm blameless.

“Honestly, I know I'm blameless. I just don't get what’s happening. I'm so over my life. It feels like it doesn't matter if you're good or bad, it all ends the same. So I've gotta conclude that God just destroys good people right along with the bad ones. When some disaster hits and people die suddenly, he just folds his arms, like he's not even bothered by innocent people suffering. He lets messed-up people run the world and puts judges in charge who don't know right from wrong. If he's not the one doing it, then who is?

“My time is running out—what's left of my life is flying by so fast I can't even see any good in it. My life is like a speedboat at full throttle, or an eagle diving for its prey. Even if I try to just forget about it, put on a happy face, and force a smile, all this pain would still be twisting my gut because it's obvious you're not going to give me a break. The verdict is already in—‘Guilty!’—so what's the point of fighting it? Even if I scrubbed myself clean with the strongest soap out there, it wouldn't matter. You'd just shove me into a mud pit or something worse, and I'd stink so bad nobody could be near me.

“God and I are not on the same level; I can't just sue him. We're never gonna be equals in a courtroom. Man, I wish there was a referee who could step in and help me get my life back on track—someone who could make God loosen his death grip on me, free me from this terror so I could just breathe. Then I'd speak my mind and tell him what's up, no holding back. But as it is now, there's just no way.”

title: God, a few questions for you...
paragraphs: I'm so over my life, I seriously hate it. I'm just gonna lay it all out, all the bitter stuff, no holding back.
Job prayed:

'Okay, God, here's the deal. Don't just call me guilty without telling me what I supposedly did. How is this 'good'? You're giving me a hard time, rejecting me—the person you made with your own hands—and then you're blessing the plans of messed-up people? You don't see things like we do. You're not fooled by how things look, right? You're not on a deadline like us. You have forever to figure things out. So what's the deal with trying to dig up dirt on me, trying to find something wrong? You know I'm not guilty. And you know no one can save me.

'You made me like a custom work of art, and now you're just going to smash me? Don't you remember how carefully you made me? Are you really going to turn me back into a pile of mud? That whole miracle of life thing, mixing everything together to make me—skin, bones, muscles, and a brain! You gave me life and so much love. You watched over every single breath I took.

'But you never told me about this part. I should've known there was a catch. Like, if I messed up even a little, you'd be on me, and wouldn't let it slide. If I'm actually guilty, I'm screwed. But even if I'm innocent, it's no better—I'm still screwed. I'm just full of bitterness. I'm drowning in this mess. I try to stay positive, to be brave, but you're just too much for me, like a lion that won't give up. You keep bringing new witnesses against me. Your anger just keeps growing, and you keep piling on the pain and sadness!

'So why did you even let me be born? I wish no one had ever seen me! I wish I'd never even existed—just a stillborn, buried without ever taking a breath. Isn't it time to just end my life? Can't you just let me be happy for a second before I die and get buried, before I'm stuck in a coffin, sealed in the ground, and sent away forever to the land of the dead, blind in the total darkness?'

title: God's Wisdom is Next Level
paragraphs: Alright, so now this guy Zophar from Naamath steps up to the plate.

He's like, 'Whoa, easy with the word vomit! Should we even let this guy keep talking? Job, for real, you think you can just go on and on, mocking everything, and we're just gonna sit here and take it? You're all like, ‘My beliefs are perfect and I’ve done nothing wrong.’ Man, I seriously wish God would just show up and tell you what's really up. I wish he’d give you a peek at what real wisdom looks like from the inside, ‘cause true wisdom is mostly an inside job. But for real, you should know you haven't even gotten half the trouble you deserve.'

'You think you can just figure out God's whole deal? Like you can draw a map of God Almighty? God is way bigger than you can even think, way deeper than you can get. He stretches further than the whole world, wider than any ocean. If he just shows up, throws you in jail, and then takes you to court, what are you gonna do about it? He sees right through people faking it, he can spot evil from a mile away—nobody's fooling him. Empty-headed guys and girls will get smart about the same time donkeys start talking.'

'But look, if you actually get your heart right with God and reach out to him, if you wash your hands of all your mistakes and kick evil out of your house, then you'll be able to face anyone without being ashamed and get a solid grip on your life, no guilt, no fear. You'll forget all your problems; they'll be like old, blurry pictures. Your life will be full of sunshine, and every dark spot will be gone by morning. You'll be full of hope and chill out, feeling confident again. You'll look around, kick back, and just relax. You'll be living large, not a single worry, and tons of people will be hitting you up for your blessing. But the people who do wrong won't see any of that. They're on a one-way street to nowhere with nothing good to look forward to—literally nothing.'

title: Job Claps Back: God's Power is No Joke
paragraphs: Job fired back:

“Oh, for sure, you guys think you’re the only experts, and when you die, all wisdom dies with you. But surprise, I have a brain too, and I’m not about to be your backup dancer. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to know this stuff.

“My own friends are roasting me, like, ‘Is that the guy who used to chat with God?’ They’re ruthless, man. ‘Look at Mr. Never-Does-Anything-Wrong!’ It’s always the people living comfy lives who are quick to judge, looking down on those who are struggling. Meanwhile, actual crooks are chilling in their gated communities, and people who couldn’t care less about God are living in luxury, like they’ve bought a personal god to protect them.

“But go ask the animals and see what they think—let them teach you something. Let the birds in the sky tell you what’s really going on. Or just listen to the earth—it’ll give you the lowdown. The fish in the ocean will tell you their stories. It’s lowkey obvious that they all know God is the one in control, that He’s got the whole world in His hands—every single living, breathing creature. Isn’t that just basic knowledge, as basic as knowing what food tastes like? You think old people have a monopoly on wisdom, that you have to be ancient to get how life works?

“Real wisdom and legit power? That’s all God. He’s the one who teaches us how to live and what our purpose is. If He tears something down, it’s gone for good. If He locks someone up, they’re not getting out. If He stops the rain, you get a drought; if He lets it pour, you get a flood. Strength and success are His to give. The person who gets played and the person doing the playing both have to answer to Him. He exposes so-called experts and makes judges look like total fools. He can take a king’s crown and make him wear rags. He strips priests of their fancy robes and fires important officials. He makes wise advisors go silent and takes away the good judgment of the elders. He throws shade on famous people and makes the strong totally weak. He shines a light in the darkest places and brings the deepest shadows into the open. He builds up nations and then lets them fall; He helps some grow and leaves others behind. He messes with the minds of world leaders until they’re clueless, sending them wandering in the middle of nowhere. They’re just stumbling around in the dark, completely lost, like a bunch of drunks.”

title: I'm Taking My Case Straight to God
paragraphs: Yeah, I've seen it all, heard it all, and I get it. Everything you guys know, I know too, so don't act like you're better than me. I'm taking my problems straight to God Almighty. I'm done with you guys, I'm going to talk to God directly. You're just spreading lies about me. You're all a bunch of fake know-it-alls. Seriously, just be quiet for once. That's the only smart thing you could do.

Alright, now listen up while I explain my side of the story. Are you gonna keep lying and say you're doing it for God? Making up stuff to defend him? Why are you always on his side? You think he needs you to be his lawyer? How would you do if you were the one being questioned? Your lies might fool some people, but they won't fool God. He'd call you out instantly if he saw you were being biased. Doesn't his greatness blow your mind? Aren't you scared to tell cheap lies in front of him? Your 'wise' sayings are just useless junk.

So just be quiet and let me talk, and then I'll deal with whatever happens. Why am I putting myself out there and risking my life? Because even if he kills me, I'll still have hope. I'll defend myself to the very end. Just watch, this is all going to work out for me. If I was guilty, do you think I'd be doing this? Putting everything on the line in front of God? You better listen to what I'm saying, for real. Now that I've said my piece, I'm sure I'll be proven innocent. Can anyone prove I'm guilty? I've said what I needed to say. I'm done.

Please, God, I have two things to ask. Grant them so I know you're with me. First, stop with all the suffering; the fear is too much for me. Second, talk to me directly so I can answer you, or let me speak and then you answer me. How many sins am I being accused of? Show me the list—how bad is it? Why are you hiding and not saying anything? Why are you treating me like your enemy? Why are you messing with me like I'm nothing? Why are you beating a dead horse? You've got a long list of mean things about me, and you're even blaming me for stuff I did when I was young. You've trapped me so I can't go anywhere. You watch every move I make and label me as a dangerous person.
Human life just falls apart, like something rotten, like a moth-eaten shirt or a moldy blouse.

title: Life's a Glitch and Then You're Gone
paragraphs: We're all in the same boat, for real: not enough days and way too many problems. We pop up like wildflowers in the middle of nowhere and then just wilt, as temporary as a cloud's shadow. Are you really going to waste your time on someone as fragile as me? Why even drag me into this whole thing? We're not much to begin with, so how do you expect us to become anything great? Mortals have a super limited time here. You've already decided how long we live—you set the limit and no one can cross it. So why not just give us a break? Ease up! Even people with the toughest jobs get a day off sometimes. For a tree, there's always hope. Chop it down and it still has a shot—its roots can sprout new growth. Even if its roots are old and gnarly, and its stump has been dead for ages, at the first hint of water it comes back to life, budding and growing like a new sapling. But us? We die and that's it. We take our last breath, and we're gone. Like lakes and rivers that have dried up, just a dusty reminder of what was once there. That's how it is for us—we lie down and never get up, never wake up again. Never. Why don't you just bury me alive, get me out of your sight until you're not so angry anymore? But don't leave me there! Set a date for when you'll come get me. If we die, do we get to live again? That's the question. Through all these hard days, I keep hoping, waiting for the final upgrade—for a resurrection! You'll be homesick for the person you created, you'll call me—and I'll answer! You'll watch every step I take, but you won't keep a list of my screw-ups. My sins will be stuffed in a bag and chucked into the sea—sunk deep in the ocean.

“Meanwhile, mountains are worn down and huge rocks break apart, stones are worn smooth and soil washes away, just like you relentlessly grind down our hope. You're too much for us. As always, you get the final word. We don't like it and our faces show it, but you send us off anyway. If our kids end up doing well for themselves, we never know it; if they do badly, we're spared the pain. Body and soul, that's all it is for us—a lifetime of pain, a lifetime of sorrow.”

title: My Friend Is Getting Called Out By His 'Wise' Friend
paragraphs: Eliphaz from Teman had to say his piece again:

“If you were actually wise, would you be talking like such a windbag, just spewing hot air? Would you be dropping nonsense in the middle of a serious convo, just babbling? Look at you! You’re making religion seem trivial, turning deep spiritual chats into empty gossip. It’s your own sin that taught you to talk like this. You basically majored in being a fraud. Your own words have exposed your guilt. It’s nothing I’ve said—you’ve incriminated yourself! Do you think you’re the first person to ever deal with this stuff? Have you been around as long as the hills? Were you listening in when God planned everything? You think you’re the only one who knows anything? What do you know that we don’t? What insights do you have that we’ve missed? We’ve got old, wise people with gray hair backing us up—people who’ve been around way longer than you. Are God’s promises, spoken so gently and tenderly, not enough for you? Why are you letting your emotions run wild, lashing out and spitting fire, putting your whole self against God by letting words like this come out of your mouth? Do you really think any human can be sinless in God’s eyes, that anyone born from a human mom can get it all together? Look, God can’t even trust his holy angels. He sees flaws in the heavens themselves, so how much less us humans, who are smelly and foul and lap up evil like it’s water?

“I’ve got a thing or two to tell you, so listen up! I’m letting you in on what I think; it’s what wise men and women have always taught, not holding anything back from what their parents taught them, back in the day when they had this land to themselves: People who live by their own rules, not God’s, can expect nothing but trouble, and the longer they live, the worse it gets. Every little sound freaks them out. Just when they think they’ve got it made, disaster strikes. They lose hope that things will ever get better—they’re on the list of people for whom things always go wrong. They wander around, never knowing where their next meal is coming from—every day is doomsday! They live in constant terror, always on edge because they insist on shaking their fists at God, defying God Almighty to his face, always fighting with God, always on the defensive.

“Even if they look super healthy, fit, and young, they’ll end up living in a ghost town, sleeping in a shack not even fit for a dog. They’ll never get ahead, never be anything special. And don’t think they’ll escape death! They’ll end up like shriveled weeds, taken down by a puff of God’s breath. There’s a lesson here: Whoever invests in lies gets lies back with interest, paid in full before it’s even due. Some investment, right? They’ll be like fruit that gets killed by frost before it’s ripe, like buds that get cut off before they can bloom. Godless people are fruitless—a barren bunch; a life built on bribes goes up in smoke. They get with sin and give birth to evil. Their lives are just wombs for breeding deceit.”

title: My Friends Are The Worst & God Is Ghosting Me
paragraphs: I’m so done with your lectures. You guys are seriously the worst at making someone feel better. Do you ever run out of things to say? What’s your problem that you just keep going? If I were in your shoes, I could say the exact same things. I could totally roast you and let you have it. But I wouldn’t do that. I’d actually try to comfort you and make things better, not worse.

It doesn’t matter if I say something or not, I still feel terrible. I’m just exhausted. God, you’ve completely wrecked me and my whole family. You’ve made me all wrinkly and gross, like you’re trying to show everyone that you’re against me. My own face in the mirror looks so messed up, it’s like silent proof of how you’re treating me. Your anger is tearing me apart, your teeth are ripping me to shreds, and your eyes are burning holes in me—God, my enemy! People look at me and are shocked. They’re disrespectful, they hit me, and they all team up against me. And God just lets it happen. He lets evil people do whatever they want to me. I was just living my life, minding my own business, and then God just beat me up. He grabbed me by the neck and threw me around. He made me his personal target, and then got a bunch of archers to shoot at me. They had no mercy and shot me full of arrows; I felt like my guts were spilling out. He attacked me again and again, charging at me like a wild bull.

I’ve basically made myself a funeral outfit and am wearing it like a regular shirt; I’m lying face down in the dirt. My face is all red and puffy from crying; you can see the dark circles under my eyes. And all this is happening even though I’ve never done anything wrong to anyone and my prayers are for real.

Oh, Earth, don’t hide the wrong that’s been done to me! Don’t silence my cries for help! There has to be someone in heaven who knows what’s really going on, some lawyer in the highest heaven who can prove I’m innocent—my Champion, my Friend, while I’m here crying my eyes out to God. I’m asking the One who speaks for people before God, just like a friend would stand up for a friend.
I only have a few years left before I go on a trip that I’ll never come back from.

title: I'm Done. My Hope is Dead.
paragraphs: I'm totally crushed, my time is up, and I'm basically staring at my own grave. Look at these haters all around me. How long do I have to deal with their disrespect?

God, for real, I need you to back me up. Like, put it in writing and sign it. You're the only one who can. These guys are useless, and you know how dumb they are. Don't let them win, right? People who turn on their friends just create more drama for their own kids down the line.

God, now everyone's talking about me. People are literally spitting in my face. My eyes are so blurry from crying, and I'm just a bag of bones. Good people are shocked and think I've totally bailed on you.
But the real ones, the people with integrity, they're holding on. They know that if they keep doing the right thing, they'll only get stronger.

Why don't you all just start over? Try again. Seriously, not one of you has said anything smart. My life is basically over. All my dreams are gone, my hopes are dead. I was hoping for a little light, but it's all dark. If all I’ve got to look forward to is a home in the graveyard, if my only hope for comfort is a well-built coffin, if a family reunion means going six feet under and the only family that shows up is worms... you call that hope? Who could find hope in that? Nah. If my hope is dead, I guess you can all come to the funeral.

title: When Your Friend's Advice is Actually a Roast
paragraphs: Then Bildad from Shuhah had to jump in:

“Bro, are we ever gonna end these word games? Seriously, let's get real. Why are you treating us like we're idiots? You're looking down on us like we don't know anything. Why are you getting so worked up? You think the whole world should change just for you? Should we just pause reality to make you happy?

“Here’s the deal: the light of a bad person gets turned off. Their flame just dies out. Their whole house goes dark—every single light. Their confident walk gets all weak and shaky, and they trip into their own traps. They get tangled up in their own drama. Their feet get caught, and they get a noose around their neck. They trip on hidden ropes and fall into holes they dug for themselves. Scary stuff comes at them from everywhere. They're running around all confused. The grave is starving and ready to eat them for dinner, like a fancy meal for Death itself. They get dragged from their cozy home straight to death row. Their life just goes up in smoke, and acid rain soaks their ruins. Their family tree dies off, and their future is gone. They won't be remembered at all—like they never even existed. They get thrown from the light into total darkness, kicked out of the world. And they leave with nothing—no kids, no legacy, nothing to show for their whole life. Westerners are stunned by their fate, and easterners are horrified, like, ‘Whoa! So this is what happens to messed-up people. This is how it ends for people who ignore God!’”
changes: Ch18: restored "acid rain soaks their ruins" (MSG 18:16)

title: God Left Me On Read
paragraphs: Job shot back:

“Yo, how long are you guys gonna keep dragging me like this, just hammering me with your speeches? You’ve called me out like, a dozen times now. Have you no chill, just shaming me like this? And even if I did mess up or get off track, how is that any of your business? Why are you so obsessed with putting me down, using my own struggles to attack me? Take it up with God—He’s the one who put me in this situation, He’s the one who trapped me in this mess.

“Look, I’m over here screaming ‘I’m being attacked!’ but no one listens. I’m calling for backup and it’s just crickets. God put up a massive wall in my way—I’m totally stuck. He switched off all the lights, so now I’m just lost in the dark. He completely wrecked my reputation and took away all my self-respect. He’s taken me apart, piece by piece—I’m toast. Then He just ripped out all my hope like a weed. He’s so mad at me, for real. He’s treating me like I’m His number one enemy. He’s launched this huge attack against me, throwing everything He’s got at me, coming at me from every direction at once.

“My own family is ghosting me; anyone who knows me is swerving. My relatives and friends are all gone; people who stayed at my house act like I don’t even exist. The maids look at me like I’m some random dude off the street, like they’ve never even seen me. I call my own assistant and he just ignores me, even when I’m literally begging him. My own wife can’t even stand being near me. My own brothers think I’m disgusting. Even the little kids on the street look down on me; when I show up, they make fun of me. All my closest friends can’t stand me; the people I loved the most have turned on me. I’m basically a walking skeleton; my life is hanging on by a thread.
“Guys, my friends, please, have some pity. God has really come down hard on me. Do you have to be so harsh too? Don’t you ever get tired of tearing me down?

“I wish everything I’m saying was written down in a book—or even better, carved into a rock forever! But I know for a fact that my Redeemer is alive, the One who will give me my life back. And in the end, He will stand on this earth. And I will see Him—even if my body is all messed up. I’ll see God for myself, with my own two eyes. Man, I can’t wait for that day.

“So if you’re thinking, ‘How can we make him see that this is all his own fault?’ just stop. You should be worried about yourselves. Worry about your own issues and the fact that God’s judgment is coming, because trust me, it’s definitely on its way.”

title: Why Wicked People Never Prosper
paragraphs: Then Zophar from Naamath had his turn.
“I can’t believe what I’m hearing! You’ve got me so worked up, my stomach is in knots. How dare you insult me like that! Well, let me tell you what I think!

“Don’t you get it? It’s been this way since the beginning of time, since Adam and Eve were first on Earth. The good times for wicked people don’t last; their godless joy is over in a second. A bad person might get world-famous, walking around like a celebrity, but they’ll end up like a pile of poop. People who knew them will be like, ‘What is that?’ They vanish like a dream you can’t remember, like a shadow that disappears in the light. Even though they were once famous, now they’re nobody, no one even notices them. Their kids will be begging on the streets, and they’ll have to give back everything they stole. They’ll die in their prime, full of youth and energy.

“They treat evil like it’s a fancy meal, rolling it around on their tongues, trying to make the flavor last—they’re like foodies for evil! But then they get terrible stomach cramps, like a bad case of food poisoning. They throw up all the rich food they ate; God makes them vomit it all out. They eat evil like it’s their diet, but it’s a deadly diet, and it kills them. They don’t get to have nice picnics by a stream with bread and cheese and cold drinks. They spit out their food before they can even enjoy it, and they can’t relax and enjoy anything they’ve worked for. And why? Because they took advantage of the poor and took things that weren’t theirs.

“People who deny God are never happy with what they have or who they are; their greed is out of control. They steal everything but can’t keep any of it. Just when they think they have it all, something terrible happens; they get a big serving of misery. After they’ve filled up on that, God gives them a taste of his anger, and they have to deal with that for a while. When they try to escape from one disaster, they run right into another one. They get beat up from every direction. They’re stuck in a nightmare, and they watch all their stuff disappear. Their lives are a complete failure—they have nothing left. God will expose all their sins for everyone to see. Their life is a total disaster, and nothing can save them from God’s anger. So there! That’s what God has planned for the wicked—that’s what they have to look forward to.”

title: Job to God: Why Do the Bad Guys Always Win?
paragraphs: Job shot back:
“Alright, for real, just listen up. Seriously, just give me that. Hear me out, and then you can go back to roasting me all you want.

“I’m not beefing with you, I’m talking to God. So is it really a surprise that I’m over His silence? Just look at me. Isn’t it messed up what’s happened? And no, don’t say a word. I don’t need your two cents. When I think about it, I’m actually shook. My whole body just tenses up. Why do the bad guys have it so good? They live long, get crazy rich, and see their kids win. They even get to chill with their grandkids. Their houses are safe, no drama, and they never get a taste of God’s discipline. Their animals are having babies left and right, no problem. They let their kids run wild, and they’re all just vibing, making music, singing, and dancing. They live a super chill life and then just pass away peacefully in their sleep. They’re basically telling God, ‘Nah, we’re good. We don’t care about you or your rules.’ Like, ‘Why should we even bother with God Almighty? What’s in it for us?’ But they’re so wrong, it’s not even funny—they’re not in charge. It’s wild to me how they can just live like that!

“But for real, how often do you see wicked people actually fail? How often does disaster hit them, or they get what’s coming to them? How often do they get wrecked by bad luck? Lowkey, not that often. You might say, ‘Well, God’s saving up their punishment for their kids.’ But I’m like, ‘No, give it to *them* right now so they know what’s up!’ They should have to deal with the consequences of their own trash behavior, feel God’s anger firsthand. What do they even care what happens to their family after they’re gone?

“But who are we to tell God how to do His thing? He’s on a whole other level. Some people die young when everything’s going great for them—healthy and living the dream. Others die all bitter, having never had a single good thing happen. And then they both end up in the same cemetery, where the worms don’t care who was who.

“Don’t play me. I know what you’re trying to do, the little schemes you’re cooking up to tear me down. You’re naively claiming that the mansions of evil bosses fall apart and all their achievements just collapse. Have you ever actually asked anyone who’s been around? Have you listened to their stories? They’ll tell you about the bad guys and girls who get away with everything, who never have to pay for all the messed-up stuff they did. Did anyone ever call them out? Did they ever have to face the music? Nah, not likely. They get these huge, fancy funerals, get buried in expensive graves, and everyone just lies about how amazing they were.
“So how are you gonna sit there and try to make me feel better with all that nonsense? Your ‘comfort’ is straight-up cap.”

title: God Doesn't Care About Your Perfect Record
paragraphs: So Eliphaz from Teman started his lecture again:

"Like, are any of us swole enough to help God out, or smart enough to give Him tips? So what if you were perfect? You think God Almighty would even notice? Even if you were a straight-A student in life, you think He'd give you a gold star? You think He's putting you on blast 'cause He's obsessed with how pure you are? Nah. It's 'cause you're a total mess, morally speaking. Your sins are, like, endless. When people needed you, you literally took the clothes off their backs. You took advantage of them when they were down bad. You wouldn't even give a thirsty person a sip of water, or a hungry person a crumb. And there you were, all high and mighty, respected by everyone, rolling in dough. You slammed the door on widows and crushed orphans without a second thought. So now you're the one who's totally freaked out, frozen in fear. The tables have turned, big time. How's it feel to be in the dark, totally lost, and drowning in problems?"

"You get that God's the boss, right? He runs the whole universe - just peep the stars! And yet you have the nerve to be like, 'What does God even know? How can He judge from way up there in the dark? He's just chilling in the clouds, how can He see us?'"

"Are you really gonna stick with that lame excuse that bad people have been using forever? And where did that get them? They died young, wiped out by floods. They were all like, 'God, leave us alone! What's God Almighty even good for?' And yet, God was the one who gave them everything. It's wild how they can even think that way."
"Good people see the wicked fail and they're like, 'Let's party!' They're so relieved, they're like, 'Finally! Our enemies are toast. Everything they had is gone.'"

"Just give in to God, make peace with Him, and everything will be chill. Let Him tell you what's up; for real, listen to what He says. Come back to God Almighty and He'll fix your life. Get rid of all the bad stuff in your house. Stop being so obsessed with money and all your fancy stuff. God Almighty will be your treasure, like, more wealth than you can even imagine."

"You'll actually enjoy being with God, the Mighty One, and you'll be able to look at Him with confidence. You'll pray to Him and He'll actually listen; He'll help you do what you said you'd do. You'll decide what you want, and it'll happen; your whole life will be lit. When people are feeling down, you'll be like, 'Hey, chin up! Be brave!' and God will save them. Yeah, even guilty people will get away, all because of God's grace in your life."

title: God, Where You At?!
paragraphs: Job shot back:

“I’m not giving up. I’m holding my ground, and my complaint is legit. It’s not right for God to treat me this way—it’s totally unfair! If I just knew where to find him, I’d go straight to him. I’d lay out my whole case, face-to-face, and give him all my arguments. I’d finally get what he’s thinking and figure out what’s going on inside his head. You think he’d just blow me off or act like a bully? Nah, he’d have to take me seriously. He’d see a straight-up guy standing in front of him, and my Judge would have to clear me of all the charges for good.
“I look for him in the East—nothing. I search in the West, but not a single trace. I go North, but he’s covered his tracks. Then I head South, but I can’t even get a glimpse.

“But he knows where I am and everything I’ve done. He can grill me all he wants, and I’ll pass with flying colors. I’ve followed him super closely, my feet right in his footprints, and I haven’t messed up once. I’ve followed every single word he’s said, and I didn’t just listen—I treasured it.

“But he’s one of a kind, the ultimate boss. Who can even argue with him? He does whatever he wants, whenever he wants. He’s going to finish exactly what he has planned for me, and whatever else he decides to do. Is it any surprise that I’m lowkey terrified to meet him? Every time I think about it, I get freaked out all over again. God makes my heart drop! God Almighty gives me the chills! I’m completely lost in the dark, like I can’t even see my own hand in front of my face.”

title: Why Do Bad Guys Always Win?
paragraphs: “Okay, so if Judgment Day isn't hidden from the Almighty, why doesn't he just tell us when it is? Like, for real. 'Cause right now, it feels like people are literally getting away with murder. They're out here stealing, lying, and cheating their way through life. They totally rip off poor people and take advantage of anyone who can't fight back. They push the helpless out of the way and bully the weak until they're scared to even exist.

The poor are basically like stray animals, digging through trash cans for their next meal. They have to survive on whatever scraps the rich leave behind. They're homeless, freezing on the streets at night with nowhere to sleep. When it rains, they're just stuck out in the open, trying to find any little bit of shelter. It gets even worse—moms have their babies snatched right out of their arms, and poor kids get kidnapped and sold. They walk around in ripped, patched-up clothes, and even when they work super hard, they're still starving. No matter how much they grind, they can never get ahead. People are literally dying all over the place, groaning in pain. The miserable are crying out for help, but it's like God isn't even listening. He just acts like nothing's wrong!

“Then you've got the people who are basically allergic to the light. They hate doing anything good or right. As soon as it gets dark, the murderers come out to play. They kill the poor and rob anyone who can't defend themselves. Creeps who are up to no good wait for the sun to go down, thinking, 'Nobody can see me now.' Burglars do their thing at night and then hide all day. They want zero to do with the light. For them, total darkness is their morning. They actually make friends with all the scary things that happen in the dark.

“They're like worthless pieces of wood floating in the water—just useless, cursed junk. As for sure as snow melts in the summer, sinners just disappear into their graves. It's like they were never even born. Worms will have a feast on them. See, nothing evil ever lasts. They're shady and prey on people who have less than them. They might act all tough and flex their muscles, but deep down, they're empty. They might feel safe for a minute, but God is watching them the whole time. They might have a few wins here and there, but then it's all over, and they have nothing to show for it. They're like yesterday's news, only good for wrapping up trash. Go ahead, try to prove me wrong. You won't be able to.”

title: God's Power is Next Level
paragraphs: Then Bildad the Shuhite had another go at Job:

“God’s in charge, and honestly, it's kinda scary how powerful He is. The whole universe? Yeah, that's all part of His master plan. You think you can count His squad of angels? Nah. Is there any spot His light doesn't reach? Double nah. So who are we, just regular humans, to think we can challenge God? How can anyone just decide they're innocent? I mean, look up. Even the moon isn't perfect, and the stars have their own issues from God's POV. So where does that leave us, regular guys and girls? We're basically like slugs and maggots next to Him. It's wild.”

title: Job to his friends: 'Wow, you're SO helpful... not.'
paragraphs: So Job replies, and he's basically like:

'Wow, you guys are a *huge* help to someone who's totally helpless. Seriously, you swooped in to save the day right on time! And the advice you're giving a guy who's completely lost? Genius. Absolutely amazing insights. Where'd you even come up with all this stuff? Who's your inspiration?'

'Down below, all the dead are freaking out, even the ones who drowned in the deepest parts of the ocean. Hell is like an open book to God, and all the graves are just uncovered holes in the ground. He stretches out the sky over nothing, and just hangs the earth in empty space. He fills up these huge clouds with water, and they don't even pop. He controls the moon, making it go through all its phases. He literally draws the line where the sky meets the ocean, separating light from darkness. When you hear thunder, that's God's voice booming. He can calm down a crazy sea storm with just his power, and he's smart enough to handle any sea monster. He just breathes and the sky clears up, and with a single finger, he can take down a giant sea serpent. And get this—that's just the *beginning*. It's like, a tiny whisper of how powerful he is. Can you even imagine what would happen if he actually decided to shout?'

title: Job's Mic Drop: Staying Real When Life Gets Messy
paragraphs: Job waited for Zophar to say something, but when he didn't, Job just went on with his own defense:

"I swear on God's life, who's totally denied me justice, the Almighty who's made my life a wreck. But look, as long as I'm still breathing, as long as God's breath is in me, I'm not gonna lie. Not one word. I refuse to admit to something I didn't do. No way I'm ever gonna agree with you guys. I'll stick to my integrity even if it literally kills me. I'm holding on tight and not letting go, and trust me, I'll never have any regrets about it.

"Let's be real, I hope my enemy gets called out for being wicked. I hope my hater is proven guilty. What future is there for the godless when they get cut off, when God pulls the plug? You think God's gonna hear their desperate pleas when everything falls apart? Did they ever even care about the Almighty? Were they ever caught praying?

"I've given you the straight-up facts about how God works, I haven't hidden anything about the Almighty. The proof is right in front of you. You can all see it for yourselves, so why are you still talking nonsense?
"I'll just use your own words against you:

"'Here's what God does to the wicked, this is what evil people get from the Almighty: All their kids will die in some crazy way; they'll never have enough food. A plague will take them all out, and their widows won't even cry. Even if they stack cash and have all the latest designer clothes, the good people will end up with the clothes and the decent folks will get the money. They build these huge houses that fall apart in one winter. They go to bed rich and wake up with nothing. Pure terror hits them like a flash flood—a tornado just snatches them up in the middle of the night. A cyclone sweeps them away—poof, gone. Not a single trace left, not even a footprint. Disasters are constantly chasing them; they run and run, but there's nowhere to hide—they just get wrecked by the storm, totally blown away.'

title: The Ultimate Treasure Hunt That's Lowkey Impossible
paragraphs: It's pretty obvious where we get valuable stuff, right? We know silver is in rocks, and we know how to get pure gold. We dig iron out of the ground and melt copper from stone. Miners go deep into the dark earth, searching the very roots of mountains for ore, digging in total blackness. They're way out, far from people and cities, just dropping down shafts on ropes. The top of the earth is for growing crops, but underneath it's a furnace cooking up sapphires and gold. The fastest birds can't see these treasures; even hawks miss them. Wild animals have no clue, and lions don't know they're there. But miners are down there, breaking through solid rock and literally ripping up mountains. They carve out tunnels and find all sorts of amazing gems. They find where rivers are born and expose all the earth's hidden secrets.

But for real, where do you find Wisdom? Where is Insight hiding? People have no idea, not the slightest clue where to even look. The deep earth says, 'Not here,' and the ocean says, 'Never heard of it.' You can't buy it with the best gold; no amount of silver is enough. Not even that famous Ophir gold can get you Wisdom, not even with diamonds and sapphires. Gold and emeralds can't compare; the most expensive jewelry is nothing next to it. Pearls and rubies? Don't even bother. All that stuff isn't even a down payment on Wisdom. You could pile up all the gold and diamonds in the world, and it wouldn't even come close to the value of Wisdom.

So where does Wisdom come from? And where does Insight live? You can't find it just by looking, no matter how deep you dig or how high you fly. Even if you ask the dead, they'll just say, 'We've only heard rumors about it.'

God is the only one who knows the way to Wisdom; He knows its exact location. He sees everything on earth, everything under the sky. After He set the winds in motion and measured out the oceans, arranged for the rain and created thunder and lightning, He looked at Wisdom and made sure it was perfect, tested and approved. Then He told all of humanity: 'Listen up! The fear of the Lord—that's Wisdom. And Insight? That's turning your back on evil.'

title: Back When I Was a Legend
paragraphs: Job just kept talking:

"Man, I’m lowkey nostalgic for the good old days, when God was really looking out for me. He’d light up the path so I could walk through the total darkness. Seriously miss those golden years when my house was blessed with God's friendship, when the Almighty was still on my team and my kids were all around me. Everything was just clicking, and nothing felt too hard.

"When I’d go downtown and chill in the main square, everyone, young and old, would give me so much respect; the whole town honored me. When I spoke, it was like a mic drop—everyone would get quiet and hang on every single word. My rep was solid; people only had good things to say. I was known for being the guy who helps people out of a jam and sticks up for those who are down bad. Dying people would bless me, and I could even bring a little comfort to those who were grieving. I kept it 100 in all my interactions. My brand was being fair to everyone. I was literally eyes for the blind and feet for the lame, a father figure to the poor, and a defender of the vulnerable. I’d snatch up thieves and make them give back what they took. I really thought, ‘I’m gonna die peacefully in my own bed, thankful for a long, full life. A life that’s stable and thriving, always fresh, with my soul full of glory and my body strong till the very end.’

"Dudes and girls would listen up when I spoke, waiting for whatever I’d say next. After I said my piece, they’d be silent, just processing it all. My advice was like a cool drink of water on a hot day—they soaked it all up. When I’d smile at them, they almost couldn't handle it; their faces would light up and their problems just seemed to disappear. I was their leader, setting the vibe and the pace for their lives. Wherever I went, they followed.
changes: Ch29: split declared for MSG 1-6 (intro + body)

title: My Life is a Total Dumpster Fire RN
paragraphs: But not anymore. Now I'm the punchline for all their jokes—these young thugs, these little punks. Seriously, I used to think their dads were total newbies, but these kids are even worse. They're like a pack of stray dogs—useless, scruffy, and always looking for trouble. They're half-starved, digging through trash in back alleys, basically just homeless guys chewing on scraps. They got kicked out of the community, labeled as troublemakers. Nobody wanted them around, so they were forced out. You could hear them at the edge of town, a whole crew of beggars and nobodies, completely rejected.

And now *I'm* the one they're targeting, treating me like dirt, taunting and mocking me. They absolutely hate me, and they're not afraid to show it. These little jerks have the nerve to spit right in my face! Now that God has totally wrecked me and I've hit rock bottom, they're going all out. There are no rules. They sneak up on me, trip me, and then kick me while I'm down. They're throwing everything they can at me to destroy me, and nobody is stepping in to help. They're just walking all over my broken life like it's nothing. It's terrifying—my reputation is ruined, and any hope I had is gone.

My life is just draining away while all this suffering takes over. At night, it feels like my bones are being chewed on; the pain is relentless. It's like I'm tied up, with a rope around my neck. I can't get comfortable. I've been thrown into the mud, and now I'm just a complete mess, inside and out.

I'm screaming for help, God, but I'm getting nothing back from you. No answer. I'm standing up to you, trying to get your attention, and you just stare at me blankly. You've become my enemy—you're just slapping me around and knocking me down. You lifted me up just to drop me from way up high, and I crashed. I know what you're doing—you're determined to kill me, to put me six feet under.

What did I even do to deserve this? Did I ever hit anyone who was calling for help? Haven't I felt bad for people with hard lives and been heartbroken for the poor? But what did that get me? I was expecting something good, but instead, I got all this bad stuff. I was looking for some light, but it's just been dark. My stomach is always in knots; it never calms down. Every single day is just more suffering. I'm walking around under a dark cloud, like the sun's gone forever. I stand up in front of everyone and just cry out. I howl like the jackals, I hoot with the owls. I'm all bruised up and burning with a fever. My fiddle plays nothing but the blues now; my mouth harp just wails laments.
changes: Ch30: FIXED mistranslation: hit not ignore (MSG 30:24)

title: I Kept It 100, I Swear
paragraphs: I made a legit pact with myself to never creep on a girl. So what does God owe me? What do I get from the Almighty? Isn't trouble for the bad guys and disaster for the ones who do wrong? Doesn't God see everything I do? Doesn't he count every step I take?
Have I been fake or hung out with liars? Test me, God, and you'll see I'm the real deal. If I've messed up, wanted things I shouldn't, or sinned, then fine, let someone else have my stuff.
If I cheated on my wife, then she can go and do the same. That's a disgusting thing to do, and I'd deserve the worst. It's like a fire that burns everything down.
Have I been a bad boss? If so, what will I say to God when he calls me out? Didn't he make all of us? We're all equal in his eyes.
Have I ignored the poor or let them starve while I ate good? No! My home was always open to them—they were always welcome at my table.
Have I let people freeze without clothes? No way! They blessed me because they knew I'd help them out.
If I ever used my power to hurt the weak, then break my arms. I'm scared of God, that's why I don't do that stuff. How could I face him?
Did I ever worship money or brag about being rich? Was I so amazed by the sun and moon that I worshipped them in secret? If I did, I'd deserve the worst punishment for betraying God.
Did I ever get happy when my enemies failed? Nope. I never even cursed them under my breath.

Didn’t my workers say, ‘He fed us well—there were always second helpings’? And no stranger ever had to sleep on the street; my doors were always open to travelers. Did I hide my sin like Adam did, burying my guilt behind closed doors, because I was scared of what people would say—scared of the neighbors’ gossip—turning myself into a recluse? You know good and well that I didn’t.

Oh, if only someone would hear me out! I’ve signed my name to my defense—now let the Almighty answer. I want to see my indictment in writing. Anyone’s welcome to read my defense—I’ll write it on a poster and carry it around town. I’m ready to account for every move I’ve ever made—to anyone and everyone, prince or pauper.

If the very ground I farm accuses me, if even the furrows fill with tears from my abuse, if I’ve ever ripped off the earth for my own profit or kicked its rightful owners off their land—then let thistles grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley.
Job was done talking to his three friends.
