title: The Intern Snaps: A New Challenger Enters the Ring
paragraphs: So Job's three friends finally went quiet. They were totally out of arguments, stuck because Job just wouldn't back down or admit he did anything wrong. That's when this guy Elihu totally lost it. (He was the son of Barakel the Buzite, from the Ram family.) He was seriously mad at Job for acting like he was more right than God. But he was also mad at the three friends because they couldn't come up with a good comeback or prove Job was wrong. Elihu had been waiting patiently while they all talked because they were older than him. But when he saw that the three dudes had nothing left to say, he just exploded.
This is what Elihu, son of Barakel the Buzite, had to say:

“Look, I'm young, and you guys are all old and have been around the block. That's why I kept my mouth shut and didn't jump into the conversation. I was thinking, 'Age equals wisdom, right? The older you are, the smarter you get.' But nope, I was wrong. It's actually God's Spirit inside someone, the breath of God himself, that gives people real understanding. The so-called experts don't have a monopoly on wisdom; just being old doesn't mean you know what's up. So, I've decided it's my turn to talk. Listen up! I'm about to tell you what I really think.

“I was hanging on every word you said, listening hard to your points. While you were trying to find the right thing to say, I was all ears. And what did you accomplish? Literally nothing. Nothing you said even got close to touching Job. And don't try to make excuses like, 'Oh, we did our best. Now it's God's problem to make him see sense.' Job hasn't even had to deal with my arguments yet. And trust me, I'm not gonna use your weak arguments!

“Are you three seriously out of things to say? Of course you are! You're total phonies! Why should I wait around any longer now that you're just sitting there, completely stuck? I'm ready to say my piece. That's right! It's my turn—and it's about time! I have so much to say, I'm about to burst. The pressure is building up inside me like a volcano. I'm about to blow. I have to speak—I've got no choice. I have to get this off my chest, and I'm gonna say it straight up—the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I've never been good at sucking up to people; my Creator would shut me down real quick if I tried that now!”
changes: Ch32: badge 6 -> 6-10 (speech intro is part of MSG 6-10); split declared

title: God's DMing You, Bro - U Missed It?
paragraphs: “Aight Job, for real, just listen up for a sec. I need you to hear what I’ve gotta say. I’ve been thinking hard about this, and I’m keeping it 100 with you, straight from the heart. The Spirit of God is the one who made me, and the breath of the Almighty is what gives me life.

“So if you think you can argue against me, go for it. Lay out your case. Stand up for yourself! Look, I’m just a person, same as you; we’re both basically made of mud. So let’s just talk this out. Don’t be intimidated by me or anything.

“I literally heard you say this with my own ears. You said, ‘I’m innocent—I haven’t done anything wrong. For real, I’m clean—my conscience is clear. But God is still picking on me; he’s treating me like I’m his enemy. He’s got me on lockdown and is watching my every move.’

“But let me tell you, Job, you’re wrong. Dead wrong. God is so much bigger than any of us. So how can you even try to drag him to court and then get salty when he doesn’t respond to your accusations? God is always responding, one way or another, even when people are totally clueless to it.

“Like, sometimes in a dream, a vision in the middle of the night when everyone’s knocked out, deep in sleep—God will whisper in their ears and hit them with some warnings. He does it to stop them from doing something stupid they were planning, from making a reckless move, and to keep them from dying young, from crossing that point of no return.

“Or, God might try to get your attention with pain, by making you so sick you’re stuck in bed. So sick that you can’t even look at food, and you have zero appetite for your favorite snacks. You lose a ton of weight, wasting away to basically nothing, just a bag of bones. You’re right on the edge of death, feeling like every breath could be your last.

“But even in that moment, an angel could show up, a real champion—and there are thousands of them—to fight for you. A messenger who would step in and mercifully call off the death sentence, saying: ‘I’ve got the payment to save him!’ And before you know it, you’re completely healed, looking healthier than ever.

“Or, you might just hit your knees and pray—and God would be so stoked about it! You’d see God’s smile and be celebrating, because you’re finally right with Him again. You’d be singing His praises to everyone you see, telling them, ‘I totally messed up my life—and trust me, it was not worth it. But God stepped in and saved me from certain death. I’m alive again! I can see the light again!’
“This is just how God works. He does this over and over. He pulls us back from the brink of destruction so we can see the light—and actually live in it.

“So keep listening, Job. Don’t interrupt—I’m not done. But if you think of something I need to know, just tell me. I’d actually love to see you proven innocent. But for now, just listen. Don’t distract me. I’m about to teach you some real wisdom.”
changes: Ch33: badge 23-26 -> 23-25 (para content is MSG 23-25 angel passage only)

title: Elihu Spits Facts: God Doesn't Mess Up
paragraphs: Then Elihu said his piece again.
“Alright, my smart friends, listen up and tell me what you think. It’s just common sense, right? Like knowing what tastes good. Let’s put our heads together and figure this out.

“We all heard Job claim, ‘I’m the good guy here, but God’s being totally unfair.’ He’s like, ‘When I stick up for myself, I get called a liar. I did nothing wrong, but I’m getting punished anyway.’ Seriously, have you ever heard anything so wild? Is this guy for real? It feels like he’s been hanging with a bad crowd and is now just repeating their nonsense, like saying, ‘There’s no point in even trying to be on God’s good side.’

“You guys are pros at this stuff, so we should be on the same page. God literally can’t do anything evil; the Almighty just doesn’t do wrong. He makes sure we get what we deserve—no more, no less. What goes around, comes around, you know? It’s impossible for God to be wicked or for the Almighty to mess up justice. He’s the one running the whole planet! He’s got the entire world in his hands. If He just decided to stop breathing, every single person would just drop dead.

“So, Job, think about it. It’s pretty obvious. Can someone who hates rules actually enforce them? Are you seriously going to blame the righteous, all-powerful God? Doesn’t God call it like He sees it, exposing corrupt leaders for the criminals they are? Do you think He gives special treatment to the rich and famous and ignores the poor? Isn’t He responsible for everyone equally? People who get what’s coming to them often die suddenly, right? And evil rulers get taken down. When the so-called ‘greats’ are taken out, you know God’s pulling the strings behind the curtain.

“He sees every single thing everyone does. He doesn’t miss a beat. There’s no darkness, no shadow, deep enough to hide people who do wrong. God doesn’t need to look for clues; their guilt is an open-and-shut case. He takes down the high and mighty without even a heads-up and replaces them with someone else. No one gets away with anything. Judgment can come overnight, super quick. He punishes the wicked for their evil out in the open for everyone to see, because they bailed on following Him and stopped caring about His ways. The cries of the poor were the evidence of their betrayal; the suffering of the needy got God’s attention.

“If God is quiet, what’s it to you? If He looks away, what can you do? But whether He’s silent or hidden, He’s still there, in charge, making sure the haters don’t take over and ruin everyone’s lives.

“So why not just come clean to God? Just say, ‘I messed up, but I’m done with that. Show me what I’m not seeing. Whatever I did wrong, I won’t do it again.’ Just because you don’t want to play by God’s rules, you think He should play by yours? It’s your call. I can’t make it for you. So, what’s it gonna be?

“Anyone with half a brain would agree—and the wise people who’ve heard me out are all on board—‘Job is being clueless. He’s talking complete nonsense.’ Job, you need a reality check for talking back to God like that. You’ve just made things worse by rebelling against God’s correction, shaking your fist at Him and just piling on more accusations against the Almighty.”

title: Does God Even Care If You're Good?
paragraphs: So, Elihu just went in on Job again.
He was like, "Does any of this even make sense? First, you're all, 'I'm totally innocent in God's eyes.' Then you turn around and say, 'It literally makes no difference if I've sinned or not.'

"Okay, hold up. I'm about to show you why you, and your friends, have no idea what you're talking about. Just look up at the sky. Take a real, long look. See those massive clouds way up there? If you sin, what difference do you think that makes to God? No matter how many times you mess up, is it gonna bother Him? And even if you're perfect, what's God getting out of it? You think He's relying on your good deeds? The only people who actually care if you're good or bad are your family, friends, and neighbors. God's not sitting there stressed about your behavior.

"People cry for help when things get tough, sure. They complain when they're getting pushed around, but they never think about God when life is good, when He's the one giving them reasons to sing. They don't pay attention when God uses all of creation, like birds and animals, to teach them stuff. People are just arrogant and don't care about God—until they're in trouble, of course. And by then, God's not listening. Those prayers are just pure panic, not real faith. The Almighty isn't paying attention to that. So why would He listen to you just because you're complaining that you're tired of waiting for Him to do something about all the problems in the world?
"Job, you're just talking nonsense. Complete and utter nonsense!"

title: God's Not a Bully (and Other Truth Bombs)
paragraphs: So Elihu took a deep breath and just kept going:

"Yo, just hang with me a little longer. I'll make you see what's up. There's still more to say for God's side of things. I got all this info straight from the Source, for real. Everything I know about what's right, I learned from my Maker Himself. Trust me, I'm giving you the 100% uncut truth; for real, I know what I'm talking about.

"Look, it's true God is all-powerful, but He doesn't just go around bullying innocent people. For the wicked, though, it's a whole different story—He doesn't give them the time of day. Instead, He stands up for the rights of those they hurt. He literally never stops watching out for the good people; He gives them major props and promotes them like crazy, forever. When things get rough, when they're hit with hard times and suffering, God lets them know where they messed up. He shows them how their own pride got them into trouble. He makes them listen to His warning and tells them they have to turn away from their bad choices. If they actually listen and serve Him, they'll end up living a long, chill life, basically on easy street. But if they don't listen, they'll get taken out in their prime and will have learned nothing about what life's really about. People who are always angry and don't have God just keep stacking up complaints, always blaming everyone else for their problems. They waste their lives on wild living and die young. But for those who learn from their suffering, God uses that suffering to save them.

"Oh, Job, can't you see it? God is trying to pull you away from the jaws of danger! He's leading you into this wide-open space, inviting you to a feast with a table full of blessings. And here you are, weighed down by the guilt of the wicked, totally obsessed with blaming God! Don't let your money fool you; you can't just bribe your way out of this mess. You really think you could buy your way out? No shot. And don't think nighttime, when people usually sleep off their problems, is going to bring you any escape. Most importantly, don't make things worse by doing more wrong things—that's the very reason you're suffering in the first place!

"Have you ever even considered how powerful God is? Have you ever heard of a teacher as great as Him? Has anyone ever had to tell Him what to do, or call Him out, like, 'Yo, you did that all wrong!'? So remember to praise the stuff He's made, which people write songs about all the time. Everyone sees it; no one is too far away to see it.
"Just take a long, hard look. See how great He is—He's infinite, bigger than anything you could ever think up or figure out!

"He pulls water up from the ocean, purifies it, and fills up His rain clouds. Then the sky just opens up and pours down these massive showers on everyone. Does anyone have a clue how that even works? How He arranges the clouds, or how He makes thunder speak? And look at that lightning! It's His personal light show that fills the sky and even lights up the bottom of the ocean. These are all signs of His power, His generosity, and His loving care. He throws lightning bolts like arrows, and His aim is perfect. The Most High God roars with thunder, showing He's angry at evil.

title: God's Weather Control is Next Level
paragraphs: Yo, whenever this stuff happens, my heart just stops. For real, I'm stunned and can't even catch my breath. Just listen to it! Listen to His thunder, that deep, rumbling sound is His voice.

He unleashes lightning from one end of the sky to the other, lighting up the whole planet. And right after, the thunder booms—that's His powerful, majestic voice. He's not holding back at all, going all out. You can't mistake that voice—His word is like this incredible thunder, and the things He does are just staggering, way beyond what we can get our heads around.

He tells the snow, 'Go blanket the earth!' and the rain, 'Soak the whole countryside!' You can't escape the weather—it's just there. And you definitely can't escape God. Wild animals run for cover, hiding in their dens when blizzards come roaring from the north and everything gets covered in ice.

It's literally God's breath that makes ice and freezes lakes and rivers solid. And yup, it's God who loads up the clouds with rain and then hurls lightning from them in every direction. He makes them do exactly what He says, all over the world. Whether it's for discipline, for grace, or just to show some insane love, He makes sure they leave their mark.

“Job, are you even listening? Have you noticed any of this? Just stop for a second! Take in all of God's insane miracle-wonders! Do you have any clue how God does all this, how He makes bright lightning come from dark storms, or how He stacks up those fluffy clouds—all these miracle-wonders from a perfect Mind? Bro, you don't even know how to stay cool on a super hot day, so how can you even think about messing with that sky that's like a blazing oven?

“If you're so smart, then teach us how to talk to God. We're completely in the dark and can't figure it out. You think I'm dumb enough to challenge God? That's just asking for trouble. No one with any sense stares right at the sun when it's bright and there are no clouds. Just like gold comes from the northern mountains, a terrifying beauty streams from God.

“Mighty God! He's so far beyond us! His power and justice are unbeatable! It's crazy to think He'd ever treat anyone unfairly. So just bow down to him with deep respect, everyone! If you're smart, you'll definitely worship him.”

title: God Finally Claps Back at Job
paragraphs: And then, God finally answered Job, but like, from the middle of a crazy tornado. He said:

“Yo, why are you making things so complicated? Why are you talking all this stuff when you have no idea what you’re talking about? Get it together, Job! Stand up. For real. I’ve got some questions for you, and I need some straight answers. Where were you when I made the Earth? Go ahead, tell me, since you’re so smart. Who decided how big it should be? You’d know that, right? Who drew up the blueprints and took the measurements? How were the foundations poured, and who put in the final cornerstone, while the morning stars were all singing together and the angels were shouting for joy? And who was in charge of the ocean when it burst out like a baby being born? That was me! I wrapped it up in clouds like a soft blanket and tucked it in for the night. Then I built a whole playpen for it, a super strong one so it couldn’t just run wild, and I said, ‘Stay here. This is your spot. All your wild tantrums have to stay in this area.’

“Have you ever, like, ordered the morning to get up? Or told the dawn to get to work? So you could just grab the Earth like a blanket and shake out all the bad guys like they’re bugs? When the sun comes up, it shows everything for what it is, all the colors and shapes. The wicked lose their cover of darkness—and they’re caught red-handed.

“Have you ever actually gotten to the bottom of the ocean, like for real? Explored all those crazy deep-sea caves? Do you know anything about death? Got any clue about its dark secrets? And do you have any idea how massive this planet is? Say something if you even have a tiny clue.

“Do you know where light comes from, or where darkness hangs out? So you could, like, take them by the hand and walk them home if they get lost? Oh, right, of course you know. You’ve known them your whole life, basically grew up in the same neighborhood, huh?

“Have you ever been to the place where snow is made? Or seen the warehouse where I keep all the hail, all the snow and hail I have ready for when things get rough, for times of war and battle? Can you find the path to where lightning comes from, or the spot where the wind starts blowing? Who do you think carves out canyons for the crazy rainstorms, and maps out the path for thunderstorms that water fields no one ever sees, deserts that are totally empty, soaking the useless wastelands until they’re covered in wildflowers and grass? And who do you think is the dad of rain and dew, or the mom of ice and frost? You don’t seriously think all this amazing weather just happens by itself, do you?

“Can you get the attention of the Pleiades sisters, or get Orion to stop his hunt for a sec? Can you make Venus look your way, or convince the Great Bear and her cubs to come out and hang? Do you even know the first thing about the constellations and how they run things down here on Earth?
“Can you get the clouds to listen to you and make it rain on command? Can you take control of the lightning and have them report to you for their assignments?

“Who do you think made the ibis so smart about the weather, or made the rooster know when a storm’s coming? Is anyone smart enough to count all the clouds or to tip over the sky’s rain barrels when the ground is all cracked and dry, baked as hard as a brick?

“Can you teach a lioness how to hunt for her prey and feed her hungry cubs while they’re just sitting in their den, starving? And who puts out food for the ravens when their babies are crying out to God, flapping around because they have nothing to eat?”
changes: Ch38: badge 1 -> 1-11 (intro line is part of MSG 1-11); split declared

title: God's Wild Kingdom is GOATED
paragraphs: You think you know it all, but do you know when mountain goats have their babies? Or have you ever seen a deer give birth? Do you have any clue how long they're pregnant? Or when it's time for them to pop out their little ones? Their babies grow up fast and then they're out, living their own lives. They just dip and never look back.

And who do you think let the wild donkey run free? Who just opened the gate and was like, 'Go for it'? That was me. I gave him the entire wilderness to just vibe in, all the open fields and plains. He's out there laughing at the city donkeys stuck doing all the work. He doesn't even hear the drivers yelling. He just chills in the hills, eating whatever green stuff he finds.

You think a wild buffalo is gonna work for you? Like, he's just gonna volunteer to sleep in your barn? Can you even picture trying to make a buffalo pull your plow and farm your fields? Yeah, he's super strong, but could you actually trust him with that? Would you really bet on him to do the job? You wouldn't trust him for a second to do what you want, when you want.

Then there's the ostrich, flapping her wings but it's lowkey useless. All those nice feathers, for what? She just lays her eggs on the ground, leaves them in the dirt out in the open. She doesn't even care if they get stepped on or crushed by some animal. She's so careless with her own kids, like they're not even hers. She literally doesn't care about anything. God didn't make her the sharpest tool in the shed, that's for sure. But when she runs? It's wild. She's so fast, she leaves horses and their riders in the dust, just laughing.

And were you the one who made the horse so majestic and gave it that awesome mane? Did you make it so it prances around and scares things with its powerful snorts? It paws at the ground, all hyped up, and then charges right into a fight. It just laughs at danger, totally fearless, and doesn't back down from a sword. All the noise of weapons doesn't even bother it. It gets amped up, and when the trumpet sounds, it just takes off. It hears the trumpet and gets all excited, smelling the battle from far away, feeling the thunder of the war cries.

Was it your idea that taught the hawk how to fly, just soaring effortlessly on thermal updrafts? Did you tell the eagle to fly high and build its nest way up on the cliffs, totally safe on some rocky peak? From way up there, it spots its food from a huge distance. Its babies eat dead animals; wherever there's a carcass, you'll see that eagle circling.

title: God's Mic Drop & The Ultimate Beast
paragraphs: God then confronted Job directly:
“So, what do you have to say for yourself? You gonna try to drag me, the Almighty, to court and press charges?”
Job answered:
“I’m speechless, lowkey in awe—words are just not coming to me. I should’ve never opened my mouth. I’ve talked way too much. I’m ready to just shut up and listen.”
Then God spoke to Job from the middle of a storm, and this is what he said:
“I’ve got more questions for you, and I want some straight answers.

“You really think you can call me out on what I’m doing? You’re calling me a sinner just so you can look like a saint? You got an arm as strong as mine? Can you make your voice boom like thunder the way I can? Go on then, show me what you got. Let’s see what you’re made of. Unleash all that anger. Go after the arrogant and knock them flat. Target the proud and make them bow down. Stop the wicked in their tracks—like, totally wreck them. Dig a huge grave and just toss them in—nameless bodies in a forgotten spot. If you can do all that, for real, I’ll step aside and let you run things. You can definitely save yourself with no help from me, right?

“Now, check out this massive beast, Behemoth. I made him, just like I made you. He’s just eating grass, as chill as a cow. But just look at the strength in his back, the crazy power in his stomach muscles. His tail swings like a giant cedar tree. His legs are like solid beech trees. His bones are basically steel; every single one is hard as iron. He’s the most magnificent of all my creatures, but I can lead him around like a little lamb. The grassy hills are his buffet, and little field mice play around him without a care. He takes his afternoon naps under shady trees, cooling off in the swamp. Just chilling in the leafy shade with the wind in the willows. And when the river gets wild, he doesn’t even flinch. He’s totally unbothered, even when the Jordan River is flooding like crazy. But trust me, you would never want this guy as a pet—you’d never be able to housebreak him!”

title: God Flexes with the GOAT of all Sea Monsters
paragraphs: “So, you think you can just reel in the giant sea monster, Leviathan, with a fishing pole and shove him in your basket? You think you can just toss a rope around him or snag him with an anchor? Is he gonna beg you for mercy or try to sweet-talk you with fancy words? You think he's gonna ask to be your servant for life? Are you gonna play with him like he's a pet goldfish? Or make him the cute little pet for the neighborhood kids? You gonna put him up for sale at the local market and let people bargain for him? You think you can turn him into a pincushion with a bunch of arrows, or stick a harpoon in his massive head? Bro, if you even touch him, you're not gonna be around to tell anyone about it. You have zero chance against a creature like that. Just one look at him would knock you out. If you can't even handle his intense stare, how in the world do you expect to face ME? Who could possibly challenge me and win? I'm the one in charge of everything—I run this whole universe!

“But let me tell you more about Leviathan, this absolute unit of a sea beast, and his incredible, powerful design. Who would even think about trying to pierce his super tough skin or try to put a bridle on those jaws? And who would be brave enough to knock on the door of his mouth, which is filled with rows of terrifying teeth? His pride is on another level; you can't even make a dent in it. Nothing can get through that tough skin—it's immune to weapons and weather. It's the thickest, toughest hide you can imagine, totally impenetrable!

“When he snorts, the world lights up like a blazing fire, and when he blinks, it's like the sun is rising. Comets shoot out of his mouth, and sparks fly everywhere. Smoke pours out of his nostrils like steam from a boiling pot. He breathes, and fires start blazing; flames literally stream from his mouth. He's pure muscle, like, perfectly sculpted. Meeting him is like a dance with death. He's strong and flexible, with no weak spots anywhere on his body—he's as tough on the inside as he is on the outside, totally rock-solid and unbeatable. Even angels run for cover when he shows up, hiding from the chaos he creates with his thrashing tail. Javelins just bounce right off his skin, and harpoons just ricochet off him. To him, iron bars are like straw, and bronze weapons are a joke. Arrows don't even make him blink; bullets make no more impression on him than raindrops. A battle ax is just a splinter of wood, and he laughs at a brandished harpoon. His belly is like armor plating—unstoppable, like a giant barge. He churns up the deep ocean like you'd boil water, and he whips the sea like you'd whip eggs. He leaves a glowing trail behind him, making you think the ocean grew a gray beard! There's nothing else on this planet like him; he has absolutely zero fear. He looks down on everyone who thinks they're high and mighty—he's the king of the ocean, the king of the deep!”

title: Job's Epic Comeback & God's Mic Drop
paragraphs: Job answered God: "Okay, I'm 100% sold. You can do literally anything. No one can mess with your plans. You were like, ‘Who’s this guy muddying the water, confusing everything when he doesn’t even know what he’s talking about—and second-guessing my plans?’ And yeah, that was me. I was just running my mouth about stuff that was way too deep for me, talking about miracles like it was no big deal. You told me, ‘Yo, listen up, it’s my turn to talk. I’ll ask the questions, you answer.’ And for real, I used to just hear about you, like gossip. But now I’ve seen you with my own eyes and heard you with my own ears. It's real. My bad, for real. Forgive me. I’m never doing that again, I swear. No more living off of what other people say."

So after God was done talking to Job, he turned to Eliphaz the Temanite and was like, "I'm so done with you and your two buddies. Seriously fed up. You guys weren't straight up with me or about me, not like my boy Job was. So here's the deal. You gotta take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my friend Job, and make a sacrifice for yourselves. Job's gonna pray for you, and I'll listen to his prayer. He'll ask me not to totally wreck you guys like you deserve for talking all that trash about me and not being real, like he was."
And they actually did it. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite did exactly what God told them to do. And God was cool with Job's prayer.

After Job prayed for his friends, God totally flipped his life around and then doubled everything he had before! All his brothers, sisters, and old friends came over to his house to party. They told him they were sorry for everything and comforted him for all the crazy stuff God put him through. And they all brought him some pretty sweet housewarming gifts.

God blessed the second half of Job's life even more than the first. He ended up with 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 teams of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys. He also had seven sons and three daughters. He named his first daughter Dove, the second one Cinnamon, and the third one Darkeyes. Lowkey, there was no one in the whole country as gorgeous as Job's daughters. And their dad was super fair, giving them the same inheritance as their brothers.
Job lived for another 140 years, long enough to see his kids and grandkids—like, four generations of them! Then he died, an old man who lived a full life.
